verses.text: Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).
Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon, the Hittite; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite;
and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.
Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath bore Reuel.
Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the members of his household, with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and went into a land away from his brother Jacob.
For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their travels couldn’t bear them because of their livestock.
Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.
This is the history of the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir:
these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; and Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.
The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.
Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the sons of Adah, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,
chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek: these are the chiefs who came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah.

These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah: these are the chiefs who came of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah: these are the chiefs who came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.
These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are their chiefs.
These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.
The children of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan’s sister was Timna.
These are the children of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
These are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father.
These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.
These are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.
These are the chiefs who came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,
chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan: these are the chiefs who came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.
These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.
Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.
Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned in his place.
Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.
Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.
Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.
Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.
Shaul died, and Baal Hanan, the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
Baal Hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.
These are the names of the chiefs who came from Esau, according to their families, after their places, and by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,
chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,
chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,
chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.

footnotes.content: I notice the Scripture takes care to trace Esau's line separately, calling him Edom. It is a reminder that the Lord records both branches of a family, even when their paths diverge from the covenant line that would carry the promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Esau chose wives from the daughters of Canaan, just as his own parents had grieved over such unions earlier. It makes me pause to see how readily we repeat the very things that once brought sorrow to those who loved us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Basemath is named as Ishmael's daughter, linking Esau's house to Abraham's other branch. The Lord is faithful to care for all the descendants of Abraham, though the covenant promises flow through a different path.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eliphaz and Reuel are born to Esau. I see the Lord granting children even to one who walked apart from the birthright blessing, for His kindness extends beyond our deserving.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three sons are born to Oholibamah in Canaan. It strikes me that Esau's household grew there for a time, but their roots would not remain in the land of promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Esau gathers his whole household and all his possessions and leaves for a land away from Jacob. What was once rivalry now becomes separation, and the Lord uses even division to order the places He has appointed for each.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their substance was too great for them to dwell together. I have learned that God often provides enough to bless both, but not always enough for both to remain in the same place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Esau settles in the hill country of Seir, and he is called Edom. Mount Seir becomes the land of his inheritance, a place the Lord would later have dealings with, yet never the land of the covenant promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The history begins again, tracing Esau as father of the Edomites in Seir. I am thankful that our God is a God who knows every family, and keeps record of those He has made.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons are named by their mothers once more, Adah and Basemath. It reminds me that the Lord sees and names each child, even in a long list of those not in the direct line of the promise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Eliphaz's sons are listed: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. Teman in particular would become known in later days for wisdom, showing how even a branch from Esau left a name in the land.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Timna bore Amalek to Eliphaz. Amalek would become a lasting foe to Israel, yet here he first appears in the family of Esau. The seeds of future conflict are quietly sown, and only the Lord knows how far they will grow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Reuel's sons are named: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. I take comfort that the God who called Abraham also cares to record each of these names for all generations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Oholibamah bears Jeush, Jalam, and Korah to Esau. Three more names added to the growing house, each one known to the Lord before they were ever known to men.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chiefs of Eliphaz are named one by one, including Amalek. Even in Edom, authority was structured by clans, yet all of it remains under the sovereign hand of the One who gives and removes kingdoms.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chiefs of Reuel are listed, showing his line also became a house of leaders in Edom. The Lord grants order and structure even to those outside the covenant land, for He is Lord over all nations.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chiefs of Oholibamah's sons are recorded. I see the faithfulness of Scripture to give dignity to each family branch, knowing the Lord cares for every tribe He has formed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chapter sums it up: these are the sons of Esau, that is Edom, and these are their chiefs. A people has become a nation, yet the promise still rests on the family of Jacob.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before Edom fully took the land, the Horites dwelt there as its inhabitants. Seir was not empty when Esau came; the Lord had allowed others to dwell there until the time He appointed for Esau's house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chiefs of the Horites are named, children of Seir. It humbles me to see how many families rise and fall, while the God who made them remains the same from generation to generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Lotan's sister Timna is named, a small detail easily overlooked. The Lord delights to preserve even these brief mentions, reminding us that no person is forgotten by Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The children of Shobal are listed with care. I find rest in knowing that the Creator knows every name of every household, from the greatest nation to the smallest clan.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anah found the hot springs in the wilderness while feeding his father's donkeys. It is a simple, humble task that the Lord chose to record, teaching this old grandparent that faithfulness in small things is not hidden from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dishon and Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, are named. Once more we see the name Oholibamah, linking the Horite and Edomite families together as they dwelt side by side.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The sons of Dishon are named: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran. Each is a man with his own house, and each is fully known by the Lord who numbers the families of the earth.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ezer's sons are recorded: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan. I am struck by how meticulous Scripture is, for it treats these clans with the same care as it does the line that would bring forth our Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Dishan's sons are Uz and Aran. A brief pair of names, yet the Lord has preserved them, reminding me that even the least-known have their place in His world.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chiefs of the Horites are listed again by name and clan. What was once a people of the land is passing its authority down, yet the day would come when Esau's house would dispossess them, just as the Lord had ordained.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before any king reigned over the children of Israel, Edom already had kings. It is a gentle reminder that God allows other nations their own rulers for a time, while reserving the true King for the people He will redeem.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bela son of Beor reigns in Edom from Dinhabah. I think of how quickly kings rise and cities are named, yet all earthly thrones are but temporary before the throne of the Lord Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bela dies and Jobab of Bozrah reigns in his place. Death comes even to kings, and it teaches an old heart to look away from perishing crowns to the crown of life that will never fade.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jobab dies and Husham of the Temanites takes his place. The succession is swift, a quiet reminder that our days are numbered and we must lean on the God who outlasts every generation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hadad son of Bedad defeats Midian in the field of Moab and reigns from Avith. Even here, God gives Edom a moment of victory, showing His common grace to nations, though His covenant mercy rests elsewhere.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hadad dies and Samlah of Masrekah reigns. Again the cycle turns: life, rule, death. How good it is that our hope is not in a man who reigns for a time, but in the Man who reigns forever.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Samlah dies and Shaul from Rehoboth by the river reigns. The mention of a river city shows Edom stretching its reach, but no earthly expansion can secure what only the Lord can give.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shaul dies and Baal Hanan son of Achbor reigns. One throne passes to another, and I am reminded that the heart of man plans, but the Lord directs the steps of every kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Baal Hanan dies and Hadar reigns from Pau, with Mehetabel his queen named by her lineage. Even in Edom, royal houses take pride in family lines, yet only the line of Christ will endure to all eternity.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The chiefs of Edom are listed by name, clan, and place, closing with the simple truth: 'This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.' The Lord has kept every record, but the greater inheritance belongs to those who are blessed in Abraham's Seed, our Lord Jesus Christ.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
